subject.title: [Bug]: /v1/responses client tools are dropped by the native Codex app-server harness

question: Should the native Codex harness treat an `item/tool/call` for a caller-provided OpenResponses function as a terminal delegated client call, rather than a normal OpenClaw-owned dynamic tool that must return content to Codex?
rationale: The Codex protocol requires a callback result for dynamic tools, while the Gateway contract needs an unexecuted client `function_call` returned to the HTTP caller. Choosing the terminal/delegation semantics is an owner-level harness contract decision before implementation.

options.title: Approve terminal delegation bridge
options.body: Register filtered client tools per turn, record their invocation for `/v1/responses`, and stop or resolve the native turn through a tested delegated-call path.

options.title: Keep native Codex unsupported for client tools
options.body: Document the harness limitation and retain the current fail-closed response until Codex gains a more suitable delegation primitive.

options.title: Pursue an upstream Codex protocol extension
options.body: Ask Codex to support a first-class deferred terminal tool-call result before implementing the OpenClaw bridge.

recommendation.title: Approve terminal delegation bridge
recommendation.body: Register filtered client tools per turn, record their invocation for `/v1/responses`, and stop or resolve the native turn through a tested delegated-call path.
